suggestions_verbatim: Ruby and Tyson try out mascot ideas during a busy Saturday service, with very different ideas of what feels welcoming.
A mysterious late-night noise makes Tyson reopen his haunted-bakery theory, while Ruby suspects a much more practical culprit.
The celebration-cake client changes the competition-themed design at the last minute, forcing Ruby and Tyson to improvise without losing the cake’s heart.
The strange item Ruby found in the freezer turns out to have a connection to a longtime neighborhood customer.
Ruby puts their new closing routine to the test when Tyson realizes he has left something essential inside the bakery.
Ruby and Tyson audition neighborhood-friendly mascot ideas, but Tyson suspects one candidate has been sneaking pastries after hours.
The celebration-cake client reveals that the neighborhood baking competition has an unexpected theme, sending Ruby and Tyson scrambling for inspiration.
Tyson tries to prove the bakery is not haunted when a trail of floury footprints appears before opening.
Ruby and Tyson test their new closing routine during a hectic evening, only to realize the mascot prototype is missing.
A regular customer asks for a sourdough loaf made from a cherished family starter, raising questions about tradition and trust.
Ruby and Tyson meet a potential bakery mascot whose enthusiasm creates more problems than either expected.
The celebration-cake customer reveals that the neighborhood baking competition will be judged by a surprisingly familiar face.
Tyson investigates another late-night bakery noise and discovers a perfectly ordinary explanation that Ruby finds far more alarming.
A rush order for sourdough forces Ruby and Tyson to test whether their new closing partnership rule works under pressure.
Fox & Flour hosts a small neighborhood tasting night to choose a seasonal pastry, and the customers divide into fiercely loyal camps.
